newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch government to drop aid for regional airports.
newsitem.headline: Dutch government to drop aid for regional airports.

text.p: The Dutch government will no longer financially support the Netherlands regional airports from the year 2000, the government said in its recent report.
Entitled "Regional Airport Strategy", the report said that the government will withdraw its shareholding from Maastricht Aachen Airport, Texel and Eelde, near Groningen.
Currently, the Dutch government is paying four million guilders a year in aid towards the operational losses of the regional airports, it stated.

The government will be assessing the financial situation of the airports in the run up to the year 2000. The government plans to compensate the airports for any losses they incur in this period by a lump sum payment, it said.
After this the government will only provide limited financial assistance for infrastructural investments, it added.

A total of 25 million guilders has already been budgeted for this compensation but the government has already stated that it is likely that this will not be enough because of the expected losses from Maastricht Aachen Airport.
In order to make the regional airports financially independent from the government the report suggested that the airports should take on a national role.

For instance, the government suggested that Maastricht should take on the role as a freight hub, Eindhoven will be an airport specialising in intra-European traffic to major cities and Eelde should be a national centre of aircraft training.

A decision has not been taken on the future of Rotterdam airport. This will depend on the route of the planned TGV track which has yet to be decided on. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
